sections.heading: What are Matrix Traversal Patterns?
sections.content: A matrix (2D grid) is stored as an array of rows, and many problems are really about visiting its cells in a particular order or transforming it in place: spiral order, diagonals, layer by layer, rotation, transposition, searching a sorted matrix and simulating cell updates. Unlike graph search (BFS and DFS on grids) or grid DP, the focus here is on index arithmetic, boundaries and in-place manipulation. Mastering a few coordinate relationships turns these problems from fiddly to mechanical.

sections.heading: When to Use It
items: Visit cells in a specific order: spiral, diagonal, zigzag, boundary, layer by layer
Rotate, flip or transpose a matrix, often in place
Modify cells based on rows or columns (set zeroes, flip and invert)
Search a matrix that is sorted by rows and columns
Simulate cell updates from neighbors (Game of Life, image smoothing)
Validate a board (Sudoku) or compare patterns along diagonals (Toeplitz)
Count or sum along rows, columns or diagonals
Keywords: matrix, grid, spiral, diagonal, rotate, transpose, in place, layer, boundary, neighbors

sections.heading: The Intuition
sections.content: A matrix is just a coordinate system, so almost every pattern is a statement about (row, column). Cells on the same anti-diagonal share r + c, cells on the same diagonal share r - c, and a layer is the ring of cells at the same distance from the border. Once you know which coordinate stays fixed and which one changes, you can write the loops directly. For transformations, draw a tiny 3 x 3 example, track where one corner goes, and the index formula follows.

rows.formula: index = r * cols + c, then r = index / cols and c = index % cols

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
items: Swapping rows and columns when allocating or indexing (Array(cols) { IntArray(rows) } versus the reverse)
Assuming a square matrix: transposing in place only works when rows == cols
Repeating the middle row or column in a spiral on non-square matrices (missing the top <= bottom and left <= right guards)
Updating cells while still reading them as neighbors (Game of Life, smoothing) without a copy or state encoding
Getting rotation direction wrong: transpose + reverse rows is clockwise, reverse rows + transpose is counterclockwise
Forgetting the empty matrix or single row and column cases
Modifying the first row or column too early in the O(1) space set-zeroes approach
Reading matrix[0].size when the input may be empty
Looping column by column on large matrices, which is slower because of memory access patterns
Using the wrong box formula in Sudoku, such as r / 3 + c / 3 instead of (r / 3) * 3 + c / 3

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
items: Matrix problems are coordinate problems: r + c is constant on anti-diagonals, r - c on diagonals, and layers are rings around the border
Spiral traversal shrinks four boundaries, with guards so a single row or column is not walked twice
Rotate 90 degrees clockwise by transposing and then reversing each row
Use the first row and column as markers, or extra bits in each cell, to do in-place work in O(1) space
For rows and columns sorted in order, a staircase search from a corner runs in O(rows + cols)
Draw a small 3 x 3 example and track one cell to derive any index formula
